newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OUB sees better second half net profit.
newsitem.headline: OUB sees better second half net profit.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd (OUB) said on Friday it expected its net profit in the second half of 1997 to be better than in the first half.
"I don't do crystal ball gazing, but I expect in terms of absolute quantum our second half numbers to be higher than in the first half," OUB president Peter Seah told a news conference.
Seah said he had been asked at the full-year results news conference in March whether the company's net profit for the full year 1997 would reach Singapore $360 million.
"I said, maybe," he said. "I think I have met that expectation."
OUB earlier reported a much better than expected 27.2 percent year-on-year rise in net profit for the six months to June 30, 1997 of S$180.85 million.
If the second half matches the first six months, the full-year net would be S$361.7 million.
Consensus analyst forecasts for the first half year results were for a rise of some 20 percent to around S$170 million.
"Clearly the numbers show we have done very well," Seah said.
"We believe this is a good story. This performance was achieved on the back of a 22.4 percent rise in loan portfolio for the group."

He said the results were helped by strong contributions from outside Singapore, which accounted for around 35 percent of profits. The biggest part of that came from Malaysia, which accounted for 16 percent of profits.
Seah said the bank was "quite comfortable with our current exposure in Thailand, just bailed out by a $16 billion rescue package put together, mainly by Asian nations, in Tokyo on Monday.
